title: Elements and Compounds
seo_title: Grade 9 Science (SNC1W): Elements and Compounds Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: The properties and changes of matter; pure substances (elements and compounds) and mixtures; physical and chemical properties and changes; the relationship between the structure of simple compounds and their chemical formulas; and the elements and compounds in household products. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Science, Grade 9: SNC1W (2022), Strand C: Nature of Matter)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science (SNC1W) worksheets on elements and compounds: pure substances and mixtures, physical and chemical properties, physical and chemical changes, chemical formulas and household chemicals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A compound is two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio.
key_sub: The formula tells you which atoms and how many: H₂O has 2 H and 1 O.
body_html:
How to think about it

Matter is either a pure substance (an element or a compound) or a mixture. An element has only one kind of atom; a compound has two or more elements joined in a fixed ratio and can only be separated by a chemical change. Mixtures can be separated by physical means such as filtering or evaporating.

Physical properties (colour, density, melting point) can be observed without changing the substance; chemical properties (flammability, reaction with acid) describe how it changes into new substances. Signs of a chemical change include a new colour, a gas, a precipitate, light or a temperature change that is hard to reverse.

Example

How many atoms are in one molecule of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆?

6 + 12 + 6

Answer: 24

Example

Is rusting iron a physical or a chemical change?

A new substance (iron oxide) forms.

Answer: chemical change

Common mistakes

  • Calling melting ice a chemical change.
  • Thinking a mixture of iron and sulfur is the compound iron sulfide.
  • Reading the subscript as applying to the atom before and after it (in CO₂ the 2 is for O only).

faq.q: Why must household cleaners never be mixed?
faq.a: Some mixtures, such as bleach with ammonia or acid, react to give toxic gases.

faq.q: What is the difference between an atom and a molecule?
faq.a: An atom is a single particle of an element; a molecule is two or more atoms joined together.

items.q: Kai sorts substances. Which one is a compound (two or more kinds of atoms bonded together)?

items.q: Ethan studies magnesium burning: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. How many oxygen atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Liam looks up nitrogen gas, N<sub>2</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 2 nitrogen = 2 atoms.

items.q: Emma writes 3H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>. How many oxygen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 3 multiplies everything: 3 × 2 = 6.

items.q: Olivia studies magnesium burning: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. How many magnesium atoms are in the reactants (left side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: What is the formula of calcium nitride?
items.e: Calcium forms Ca<sup>2+</sup> and nitrogen forms N<sup>3−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.

items.q: Owen writes 3C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O. How many hydrogen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 3 multiplies everything: 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q: Emma writes 3C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>. How many carbon atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 3 multiplies everything: 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: What is the formula of lithium phosphide?
items.e: Lithium forms Li<sup>+</sup> and phosphorus forms P<sup>3−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.

items.q: Ethan studies making salt: 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl. How many chlorine atoms are in the products (right side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Sr<sup>2+</sup> and F<sup>−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 1 × (+2) + 2 × (−1) = 0.

items.q: Noah studies rusting of iron: 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3. How many oxygen atoms are in the products (right side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 6.

items.q: Emma looks up glucose (sugar), C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 6 carbon + 12 hydrogen + 6 oxygen = 24 atoms.

items.q: What is the formula of barium chloride?
items.e: Barium forms Ba<sup>2+</sup> and chlorine forms Cl<sup>−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.

items.q: Chloe looks up oxygen gas, O<sub>2</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?
items.e: 2 oxygen = 2 atoms.

items.q: Maya writes 2H<sub>2</sub>O. How many oxygen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 2 multiplies everything: 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: Mateo writes 4C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>. How many hydrogen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 4 multiplies everything: 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: Noah studies making ammonia: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3. How many nitrogen atoms are in the products (right side)?
items.e: Multiply each coefficient by the subscript and add. The number is the same on both sides: 2.

items.q: Ava looks up ozone, O<sub>3</sub>. How many atoms are in one molecule?

items.q: Na<sup>+</sup> and P<sup>3−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 3 × (+1) + 1 × (−3) = 0.

items.q: Zoe writes 4NH<sub>3</sub>. How many nitrogen atoms are there in all?
items.e: The coefficient 4 multiplies everything: 4 × 1 = 4.

items.q: Red cabbage juice is a natural indicator. What colour does it turn in soap solution (an alkali)?
items.e: Red cabbage juice is red or pink in acids and green or yellow in alkalis.

items.q: Butterfly pea flower tea is a natural indicator. What colour does it turn in soap solution (an alkali)?

items.q: What kind of bond forms between phosphorus (P) and iodine (I)?
items.e: Two non-metals share electrons.

items.q: Turmeric solution is a natural indicator. What colour does it turn in lime juice (an acid)?

items.q: What kind of bond forms between copper (Cu) and sodium (Na)?
items.e: Metal atoms share a sea of electrons.

items.q: What kind of bond forms between chlorine (Cl) and nitrogen (N)?
items.e: Two non-metals share electrons.
